seo.description: Visit Sidi Yahya oasis near Oujda: palm groves, thermal springs, quiet atmosphere and a peaceful half-day escape from the city.
seo.og_description: A palm-fringed oasis with thermal springs just a short drive east of Oujda.

name: Oasis de Sidi Yahya
hero_subtitle: A quiet palm oasis with thermal springs a few kilometres east of Oujda – local, green and peaceful.

overview.title: An Unexpected Green Pocket
overview.p1: Sidi Yahya is a small oasis and sacred site on the eastern edge of Oujda. Surrounded by palm trees and fed by natural springs, it offers a surprising contrast to the dry plains around the city. Locals come for the water, the shade and the calm.
overview.p2: The springs have been known since ancient times and were already used in the Roman period. Today the site remains modest and authentic – there is no large tourist infrastructure, which is part of its charm.
overview.p3: A visit works well as a short half-day trip from the centre, especially if you want a quieter alternative to the beach or the mountains.

moods.title: When to Visit Sidi Yahya
moods.subtitle: Best enjoyed when the light is soft and the heat is manageable.

1.title: Fresh and Quiet
1.desc: Cooler temperatures and fewer people. Ideal for a peaceful walk and photos.

2.title: Golden Light
2.desc: The palms catch warm light and the atmosphere is relaxed. Combine with a stop for tea if available.

3.title: Avoid the Peak Heat
3.desc: In summer the oasis can feel hot despite the shade. Prefer morning or late afternoon.

food.title: What to Eat Nearby
food.p1: Facilities are limited. Bring water and perhaps a small snack, or plan to eat back in Oujda.
food.li1: Water and soft drinks if local vendors are present.
food.li2: Simple snacks from small stalls on busy days.
food.li3: Return to Oujda for karan, grills or a proper restaurant meal.
food.li4: Some visitors combine the oasis with a picnic in the shade.
food.li5: Always carry bottled water, especially in the warmer months.
food.p2: Do not expect a full restaurant on site. The oasis is about nature and calm, not dining.

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: About 7 km east of central Oujda. Take a petit taxi or arrange a short private transfer. Agree the price before departing.

2.title: What to Bring
2.desc: Comfortable shoes, sun protection, water and a modest outfit out of respect for the local and sacred character of the site.

3.title: Respect
3.desc: This is a place used by locals and has religious associations. Be discreet with photos of people and keep noise low.

q1.question: Is Sidi Yahya free to visit?
q1.answer: Access is generally free or requires only a small local contribution. There is no formal ticket office.

q2.question: How far is it from Oujda?
q2.answer: Approximately 7 km east of the city centre – about 15–20 minutes by taxi.

q3.question: How long should I spend there?
q3.answer: 1 to 2 hours is enough for a walk, photos and some quiet time under the palms.

q4.question: Is it suitable for children?
q4.answer: Yes, as long as you bring water and sun protection. It is a calm, open space.

q5.question: Can I swim in the springs?
q5.answer: The springs are mainly for local use and contemplation. Do not assume swimming is allowed; follow any local rules and respect the site.
